title: Fidelity configured-capacity exactness fence
objective: Close the demonstrated FidelityManager maxRegisteredEntities numeric-domain gap so the configured registration budget remains an exact positive integer rather than accepting aliased IEEE-754 integer values, without changing F0-F4 policy or inventing an unmeasured device-memory ceiling.
acceptance: maxRegisteredEntities remains a primitive positive finite integer and additionally rejects values above the exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary 9007199254740991
the exact safe-integer boundary is accepted and one-over is rejected before manager state construction or registration accounting
default maxRegisteredEntities remains 4096 and existing small custom-capacity behavior remains unchanged
do not invent a lower practical memory ceiling without measured profiling evidence; record that as a separate performance-budget dependency if needed
preserve retained Fidelity transition atomicity, per-entity reentrancy, cross-entity isolation, policy semantics, metrics, and plain-data/no-execute validation
add deterministic source-only regressions for exact-boundary acceptance/rejection; no Studio or timing claim
notes: Capacity-mined against retained Fidelity generation-4 PR #385 exact head 827ce0cf63ca5f322502de883beb9f43581c69f2 and stacked completion PR #398. The retained source validates maxRegisteredEntities as number >=1, <math.huge, and equal to math.floor(value), but has no <=9007199254740991 exactness fence. Existing tests cover a small custom capacity of 1 and runtime over-cap rejection only. Docs call maxRegisteredEntities a configurable hard budget (4096 default). This proposed leaf is intentionally dependent on HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY DONE so it cannot overlap retained #385/#398 or bypass the separately owned trusted-history/pr-ownership recovery.
